html:
A political movement in the People's Republic of China launched by Mao Zedong in 1966 and ended by his death in 1976. Its stated goal was to purge capitalist and traditional elements from Chinese society. In practice it let Mao destroy his rivals in the party, and it brought a decade of violence and chaos.

After the disaster of the Great Leap Forward and the famine, Mao had lost ground to more practical leaders such as Liu Shaoqi and Deng Xiaoping. In 1966 he called on the young to attack "bourgeois" elements inside the party. Students formed Red Guard units, waving the little red book of his quotations.

What followed:

  • Teachers, officials, writers and anyone with the wrong class background were beaten, paraded and sent to labour camps; many were killed or driven to suicide.
  • Temples, books, art and old buildings were smashed as part of the "Four Olds".
  • Schools and universities closed for years.
  • Rival Red Guard factions fought each other, and the army had to restore order.
  • From 1968 millions of urban youth were sent down to the countryside.

Liu Shaoqi died in prison; Deng was purged twice. Lin Biao, Mao's chosen heir, died in a plane crash in 1971 after a reported plot. Estimates of the dead range from hundreds of thousands to two million or more.

After Mao died, the Gang of Four, led by his widow Jiang Qing, was arrested. The party later called the movement a catastrophe. Deng's reform and opening was in part a reaction to it.
